newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK inflation creeps up in September, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: HK inflation creeps up in September, seen rising.

text.p: Inflation crept up in Hong Kong in September to 5.2 percent on the year and economists say they expect to see a further acceleration in the fourth quarter.

Census and Statistics Department figures on Thursday showed the Consumer Price Index (A), Hong Kong's broadest measure of inflation, rose 5.2 percent on the year. It rose 4.9 percent in August, the lowest increase for nine years.
"I expected it to rise because the previous month's figure had been low due to low food prices," George Leung, economic adviser at Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd, said.
A government spokesman said higher fresh vegetable and clothing prices were largely responsible for pushing the index higher last month.
"Five point two percent is a low figure," Leung said, "especially when Hong Kong's economy is a recovery stage. Lower inflation will help it recover."
Leung saw inflation hovering around six to seven percent at the end of the year and forecast 1996 inflation at about 6.5 percent.
K.K. Chan, chief economist at Nomura Research Institute, forecast an inflation rate of six percent in the fourth quarter.
Last year, inflation stood at 8.7 percent and gross domestic product (GDP) grew a real 4.6 percent.
The government forecasts GDP growth of 4.7 percent and inflation of 6.8 percent for 1996.
